officialTitle: Ribociclib plus endocrine therapy for premenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive, advanced breast cancer (MONALEESA-7): a randomised phase 3 trial
setting: First-line advanced endocrine-based therapy (up to one prior line of chemotherapy for advanced disease permitted)

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between Dec 17, 2014, and Aug 1, 2016, 672 patients were randomly assigned: 335 to the ribociclib group and 337 to the placebo group.
design.notes: Premenopausal women aged 18-59 years; no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor. Endocrine partner tamoxifen or a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, all with goserelin.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding ribociclib to endocrine therapy with ovarian suppression improve outcomes in premenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer?

pico.population: Premenopausal women (18-59 years) with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor
pico.intervention: Ribociclib plus tamoxifen or non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, with goserelin
pico.comparator: Placebo plus tamoxifen or non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, with goserelin
pico.outcomes: Primary: investigator-assessed PFS. Key secondary: OS; safety

arms.label: Ribociclib + endocrine therapy + goserelin
arms.regimen: Ribociclib plus tamoxifen or non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor (letrozole or anastrozole), with goserelin
arms.dosing: Ribociclib 600 mg/day 3 weeks on/1 week off; tamoxifen 20 mg daily or letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg daily; goserelin 3.6 mg SC day 1 of every 28-day cycle
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via interactive response technology to receive oral ribociclib (600 mg/day on a 3-weeks-on, 1-week-off schedule) or matching placebo with either oral tamoxifen (20 mg daily) or a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor (letrozole 2·5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg, both oral, daily), all with goserelin (3·6 mg administered subcutaneously on day 1 of every 28-day cycle).

arms.label: Placebo + endocrine therapy + goserelin
arms.regimen: Placebo plus tamoxifen or non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor (letrozole or anastrozole), with goserelin

publications.title: Ribociclib plus endocrine therapy for premenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive, advanced breast cancer (MONALEESA-7): a randomised phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Primary PFS analysis

publications.title: Overall Survival with Ribociclib plus Endocrine Therapy in Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Protocol-specified interim OS analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Per investigator's assessment, median progression-free survival was 23·8 months (95% CI 19·2-not reached) in the ribociclib group compared with 13·0 months (11·0-16·4) in the placebo group (hazard ratio 0·55, 95% CI 0·44-0·69; p<0·0001).

The estimated overall survival at 42 months was 70.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 63.5 to 76.0) in the ribociclib group and 46.0% (95% CI, 32.0 to 58.9) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for death, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.95; P = 0.00973 by log-rank test).

The survival benefit seen in the subgroup of 495 patients who received an aromatase inhibitor was consistent with that in the overall intention-to-treat population (hazard ratio for death, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.98).

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 or 4 adverse events reported in more than 10% of patients in either group were neutropenia (203 [61%] of 335 patients in the ribociclib group and 12 [4%] of 337 in the placebo group)
Serious adverse events occurred in 60 (18%) of 335 patients in the ribociclib group and 39 (12%) of 337 in the placebo group

safety.description: Treatment discontinuation because of adverse events
safety.sourceQuote: 12 (4%) of 335 patients in the ribociclib group and ten (3%) of 337 in the placebo group discontinued treatment because of adverse events.

strengths: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial dedicated to premenopausal women
Significant OS benefit at a protocol-specified interim analysis
limitations: Tamoxifen partner subgroup not separately reported in these abstracts

clinicalImplications.text: Supports ribociclib plus ovarian suppression and endocrine therapy as first-line treatment for premenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with an overall survival benefit.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Premenopausal patients deserve the same CDK4/6-based first-line approach — pair with ovarian suppression; the OS benefit was seen in the aromatase inhibitor subgroup.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMID 29804902 (primary PFS) and PMID 31166679 (interim OS).
